entries.aiStanceLine: Due to a 79-point gap-up fuelled by the Labour Market Report, 86% of the 134.4-point ADR already consumed, and a crowded-short GBP positioning that could squeeze sterling higher and cap the index, upside breakout chases above 10,520 carry poor risk-reward — the macro is bullish but the range is spent.
aiBullets: The 79-point gap (0.75%) alone consumed ~59% of the 134.4-point ADR before the ORB even formed — meaning the ORB range of 47.3 points then burned another ~35%, leaving roughly 18 points of typical daily budget for the rest of the session.

Copper +2.86% and Brent +0.77% together support the two heaviest commodity blocs (miners + energy), but their bullish impulse is already priced into the gap — sector tailwinds do not automatically generate fresh intraday range.

The crowded-short GBP (COT net: -72,474, at the 89th percentile over 20 days) is a latent ceiling: a sterling short-squeeze would flip GBP bullish, which via the FTSE sign-flip becomes a headwind for the index at the worst moment for breakout longs.

Prior-day high 10,589.4 sits ~57 points above current price (10,531.9) — more than three times the remaining ADR budget (~18 pts) — confirming the mechanical R7 signal: PDH is a stretch target only and should not anchor long profit targets today.
